entries.title: John 17:1
segments:
Lifting up his eyes to heaven, he said. The words of Jesus in this chapter have often been called his high-priestly prayer.  In it he assumes the high-priestly office and function, but in a unique sense, offering himself as a sacrifice for the sins of the world.
 

 
Glorify thy Son, that the Son may glorify thee. He prays that the Father may glorify him by accepting the offering of his life and may raise him from the dead in order that, risen and ascended, he may show forth the glory of the Father by the regeneration of mankind.

entries.title: John 17:3
segments: This is life eternal. The knowledge of God and Jesus Christ which is here declared to be eternal life is that which becomes the inspiration and spiritual guide of the believer's life.

entries.title: John 17:4
segments: I glorified thee on the earth. By an obedience that was perfect.

entries.title: John 17:5
segments: Which I had with thee before the world was. Implying the deity of Jesus.
contain the prayer of Jesus for himself.

entries.title: John 17:6
segments: Manifested thy name. Jesus Christ was God 'manifested in the flesh' (

entries.title: John 17:9
segments: I pray for them.

contains Christ's prayer for his apostles.
 

 
Not for the world. His prayer for the world is in

entries.title: John 17:10
segments: All things that are mine are thine, etc.  The words of this verse are an unqualified affirmation of the equality of Jesus Christ with God.

entries.title: John 17:11
segments: In thy name. By thy power keep them in love and obedience.

entries.title: John 17:12
segments: The son of perdition. Judas Iscariot. 'Iscariot' means a man of Kerioth, a town of Judea.

entries.title: John 17:13
segments: That they may have my joy. That they, by my teaching and example, may fully partake with me in the joy I have in Thee.

entries.title: John 17:14
segments: I have given them thy word. I have manifested Thy nature unto them in my life and work.

entries.title: John 17:15
segments:
Not that thou shouldest take them from the world. It was necessary for the apostles to remain and carry on the work; but therein were their discipline and spiritual strengthening.
 

 
Keep them from the evil one. That they might effectually do what was commanded them.  Temptations were to be avoided, but when met with, overcome; persecution was to be endured without weakening their faith.

entries.title: John 17:16
segments: They are not of the world. As believers in him they shared the world's hatred of him.

entries.title: John 17:17
segments: Sanctify them in the truth. Consecrate them to the truth, to the work of preaching the gospel I have declared unto them and to the world, and to the organization of the kingdom in its earthly relations and requirements.

entries.title: John 17:19
segments: For their sakes I sanctify myself. By the offering of himself, the high priest of humanity, in voluntary sacrifice for the sins of mankind and an abiding example unto their salvation.

entries.title: John 17:20
segments: Neither for these only do I pray.
contain Christ's prayer for believers and the world generally.

entries.title: John 17:21
segments: That they may all be one, etc.  The outstanding fact of our Lord's prayer for the unity of believers is that it may be spiritual, in the Father through him.

entries.title: John 17:22
segments: The glory which thou hast given me, etc.  The glory which he has by being one with the Father they also have by being one with the Father through him.

entries.title: John 17:23
segments: That the world may know. May be convinced of the truth by the spiritual unity of the followers of Jesus Christ.

entries.title: John 17:24
segments: May behold my glory. As he prayed that those whom his Father had given him might be with him where he was, they would not only behold his glory but be partakers thereof.

entries.title: John 17:26
segments: Made known unto them thy name. Manifested Thy nature.
